ac:rich-text-body.p: Set up and operate the private LiveLabs QA Hub VM. Approved users connect through Oracle VPN, open one private HTTPS endpoint, run either the weekly PAR audit or the nightly/targeted overall regression in Jenkins, and review the resulting reports.

tr.td: Oracle VPN to a private OCI VM; no public IP
CrowdStrike Falcon configured and active before Jenkins starts
Weekly PAR audit and nightly overall regression

ac:rich-text-body.p: The deployment builds custom Jenkins and report-portal container images from common/qa-automation. It does not need a custom OCI VM image.

p: The OCI or network administrator must provide an Oracle Linux 9 VM in a private subnet with no public IP, Oracle VPN routing, and OCI NSG ingress from the approved VPN CIDR only to TCP 32222 for SSH and 32443 for the QA portal. The VM also needs approved outbound HTTPS through an OCI NAT gateway or managed proxy for GitHub, container registries, package repositories, LiveLabs, CrowdStrike, and optional OCI services. The approved Falcon sensor RPM and CID must be available securely, or the base VM must already have a configured and active sensor. Add an internal DNS record and internal CA certificate before team use.

ac:rich-text-body.p: Do not allow 0.0.0.0/0, expose standard service ports, or point public DNS at this VM. Jenkins uses internal port 32080 and the portal uses internal port 32444; neither is published directly.

p: Create a separate local security-token profile named VM-QA-hub. Do not send or commit API keys, security tokens, private keys, or passwords.

OCI CLI can return the VM private IP. The internal DNS name and approved Oracle VPN CIDR must come from the network administrator. Provisioning also needs the compartment, subnet, NSG, image, shape, and SSH public-key inputs.
SSH to the VM as the non-root account that will own the checkout:

ac:structured-macro.ac:plain-text-body: git clone https://github.com/oracle-livelabs/common.git cd common/qa-automation/deploy/vm bash install.sh \ --private-address <VM_PRIVATE_IP> \ --host <INTERNAL_DNS_NAME> \ --vpn-cidr <APPROVED_ORACLE_VPN_CIDR> \ --crowdstrike-rpm /secure/falcon-sensor.rpm \ --crowdstrike-cid-file /secure/falcon-cid

p: Run the script without sudo. It installs or verifies CrowdStrike first and refuses to start Jenkins unless Falcon has a valid CID and is active. It then installs the remaining dependencies, creates ignored local configuration and credentials, builds and starts the containers on non-standard ports, verifies the health endpoint, enables automatic startup after reboot, and prints all access URLs.
The permanent setup assumes this package has reached oracle-livelabs/common:main. Jenkins defaults to the original repository and */main; do not leave a personal fork configured on the shared VM.

ac:structured-macro.ac:parameter: Inspect the VM before opening a PR

ac:rich-text-body.p: A ZIP of the local deployment folder can start the private portal and Jenkins interface before a PR is opened. Jenkins test jobs still clone their test code from Git. Push the topic branch to a fork and set QA_GIT_URL and QA_GIT_BRANCH in the ignored VM .env for a real pre-merge run. No PR or merge is required. Restore the original repository and */main before shared use.

p: If internal DNS is not ready, omit --host. If the host firewall is managed centrally, omit --vpn-cidr.

The first run prints generated Jenkins and report credentials once. Store them in the approved secret manager. Replace the temporary 30-day self-signed certificate in deploy/vm/secrets/tls.crt and deploy/vm/secrets/tls.key with the internal CA certificate and key, then restart the portal.

ac:structured-macro.ac:plain-text-body: cd common/qa-automation/deploy/vm bash scripts/compose.sh restart portal bash scripts/healthcheck.sh

p: Public catalog checks do not need a LiveLabs account. For approved private content, retrieve the QA account from the secret manager and enter it without placing values in shell history:

ac:structured-macro.ac:plain-text-body: cd common/qa-automation/deploy/vm umask 077 read -r -p "LiveLabs QA username: " livelabs_user read -r -s -p "LiveLabs QA sign-in secret: " livelabs_secret printf '\n' printf '%s' "$livelabs_user" > secrets/livelabs-username printf '%s' "$livelabs_secret" > secrets/livelabs-secret unset livelabs_user livelabs_secret bash scripts/compose.sh up -d --force-recreate jenkins portal

p: Set QA_AUTH_TARGET_URL in the ignored .env file when scheduled jobs must establish a private session. Never place either sign-in value in .env, Git, a Jenkins parameter, or a command-line argument.

ol.li: Use the report account for the landing page and reports.
Open /jenkins/ and use the Jenkins account to run tests.

p: To print the non-secret URLs and usernames again:

ol.li: Keep CATALOG_MAX_PAGES=250 and leave CATALOG_MAX_ITEMS blank to crawl the complete catalog.
Select Build, then open /par/ after completion.

p: Start with par-catalog-not-working.csv. Review unverified and incomplete-scan CSVs separately. The audit discovers PAR links from crawled workshops and LiveStacks; no manually maintained PAR link file is required.

ol.li: Leave CATALOG_MAX_ITEMS and CATALOG_ITEM_IDS blank for the complete catalog, or enter comma-separated generated item IDs for a targeted rerun.
Select Build, then open /regression/ after completion.

p: Use the HTML report for human triage and results.csv for automation or Codex analysis.

ac:structured-macro.ac:parameter: Update the VM after changes reach main

ac:structured-macro.ac:plain-text-body: cd common git pull --ff-only cd qa-automation/deploy/vm bash install.sh \ --private-address <VM_PRIVATE_IP> \ --host <INTERNAL_DNS_NAME> \ --skip-packages

ac:rich-text-body.p: The installer is safe to rerun and retains existing Jenkins history, reports, and secrets.

ac:structured-macro.ac:plain-text-body: cd common/qa-automation/deploy/vm bash scripts/healthcheck.sh bash scripts/compose.sh ps bash scripts/compose.sh logs --tail=200 jenkins bash scripts/compose.sh logs --tail=200 portal sudo systemctl status livelabs-qa.service

ac:rich-text-body.p: If the page is unreachable, check Oracle VPN, internal DNS, the OCI NSG, the host firewall, the local health check, and then the container logs.

ul.li: No public VM IP and no public DNS.
No 0.0.0.0 bind and no exposed standard ports. Use private 32222 for SSH and 32443 for the portal.
Keep Jenkins 32080 and portal 32444 internal to the container network.
Do not start Jenkins unless CrowdStrike Falcon is configured and active.
Never commit .env, deploy/vm/secrets/, credentials, TLS private keys, or raw PAR URLs.
Use an OCI instance principal for optional private Object Storage publishing.
Back up Jenkins and report volumes according to the VM backup policy.
